thesis: The market prices November headline CPI YoY at about 3.85% (the 50% crossing sits between the 3.8 and 3.9 strikes), but three independent arithmetic routes all land near 4.2%. September NSA headline was already +3.74%, and SA headline has run +0.07%, +0.40%, +0.65% over Jul-Aug-Sep — a trailing 3-month pace of +0.37%/mo. Carrying that forward off the unusually weak November 2025 base of 325.063 gives +4.22%; a decomposition route (3.72% + 0.74% of 2026 Oct-Nov momentum − 0.25% of 2025 Oct-Nov momentum) gives +4.21%; a weighted bottom-up with core at +0.28%/mo and energy lifted by crude gives +4.20%. A YES needs only a +0.27%/mo pace against an actual +0.37%.
key_risk: The strike is strict: strike_type is `greater` on a one-decimal figure, so a reported 4.0% resolves NO and only 4.1%+ pays. My central estimate of 4.2% is just over one tenth above that line, which means a single soft energy month — gasoline fell from a $4.478 Sep peak to $4.269 and could keep sliding if crude gives back its late-October spike — flips the outcome. Headline sits 1.17pp above core (3.74% vs 2.57%), so this is an energy-driven call, and energy is the most mean-reverting component in the index. This is also a hold-to-resolution binary: the risk is the entire 33c premium, not a stop level.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the market is not making an arithmetic error at all — it is pricing an energy give-back that my trend extrapolation ignores, and with 32k contracts of open interest at this strike the pricing is not thin or inattentive. A fair reading is that the market expects the late-October crude spike to $103-110 to prove transitory and gasoline to resume falling, which would hold November m/m near +0.2%. My answer is that the direction of the lag runs the other way: retail gasoline follows crude with a two-to-four week delay, so October gasoline being flat-to-down at $4.31 against September average $4.355 reflects the pre-spike crude of roughly $95, and the move to $103+ has not yet passed through. But if crude round-trips back under $95 in early November, this idea is wrong and should be exited rather than held.

evidence.detail: Resolution date verified on two fetched sources, not from memory: the Kalshi market record gives close_time 2026-12-10 and the Robinhood event page states December 10, 2026, resolving on BLS CPI-U for the twelve months ending November 2026.

Fair value computed three ways, all ~4.2% YoY against a 4.0% strike. (1) Level: SA Nov 2025 = 325.063; carrying SA Sep 2026 of 336.298 forward at the trailing 3-month +0.37%/mo gives 338.79 = +4.22%. (2) Decomposition: 3.72% + 0.74% − 0.25% = +4.21%, where the 2025 Oct-Nov comparison window grew only +0.25% total. (3) Bottom-up: core +0.28%/mo at 79% weight plus energy at 6.5% weight with gasoline passing through crude = +4.20%. Break-even pace for YES is +0.27%/mo.

The energy-reversal objection, answered with fetched prices rather than asserted away: WTI closed $103.37 on 2026-10-27, up from $94.99 on 10-12 and peaking $110.01 on 10-19, so crude is above $100 going into November. Retail gasoline at $4.269 on 10-26 still reflects pre-spike crude, so the pass-through is ahead rather than behind.

thesis: Bitcoin broke down on 2026-10-30 — open 80,769 to a 76,338 low, a 4,431 true range worth 2.26 ATR — and now sits 1.4% above a confluence of its SMA100 (76,275) and that low. The structural point is what lies beneath: across 180 days of closes BTC spent only 17 days between 65k and 75k against 64 days in the 60-65k band, so a break of 76,275 opens an air pocket with almost no time-based support until 65k. The driver is a verified, dated confidence shock rather than a chart pattern — the largest crypto theft on record at the largest exchange, with withdrawals suspended and resumption phased in over this weekend — compounded by $643m of spot-BTC-ETF outflows on 10-30, the largest single day since June.
key_risk: The catalyst is genuinely two-sided and could resolve against this within 48 hours: if Binance resumes withdrawals without incident, the fear premium unwinds and BTC rips off a confluence support that thousands of others can also see, which is precisely why the entry is a conditional stop below 76,275 rather than a short at the market. Beyond that, this is a leveraged weekend position in an asset with no halts, where a 2.26 ATR day just happened — a gap through the 80,900 stop is a real possibility and the loss can exceed the intended risk. Micro sizing at 1.5% is the control. Separately, Robinhood availability is verified only from secondary sources because Robinhood's own futures article 404s today; confirm the contract is listed in the app before placing the order.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that a hack is a custodian failure, not a protocol failure: Bitcoin itself produced blocks normally throughout, Binance has pledged to cover all losses from SAFU and company funds and has already covered 80%, roughly $3bn was frozen, and customer balances were never touched. On that reading, 10-30 was a liquidation-driven flush into visible support and the trade is shorting the low. I do not think the evidence resolves this, and I am not claiming it does — which is why counter_argument_answered is deliberately absent from the evidence list and conviction is 4 rather than 5. What I will say is that the two channels are separable: the $643m of ETF redemptions is institutional distribution through US-listed funds and is independent of whether Binance makes its own users whole, so a clean resumption removes one pressure but not the other. And note $3bn frozen is not $3bn recovered.
